scope: 3.3.4. Feature importance shifts and real-time control implications

matched: 87 (F/M importance for water level rises by 87%)

formula_completeness.note: No standalone mathematical equations in Section 3.3.4; all parameters and numerical values formatted in KaTeX

matched: Confining SHAP analysis to feasible region changes several importance rankings with operational meaning (Tables S5-S7)
Shifts are not artefacts: most damaging conditions (SRT > 100 days, MLSS > 7500 mg/L, HRT > 10 h) excluded by output constraints, making shorter-timescale sources of variability dominant
F/M importance for water level rises by 87% from rank 5 to rank 4
In full dataset, extreme SRT and high MLSS dominate level variance and mask organic loading; in feasible region where both are moderate, F/M emerges as main driver following batch production schedule
Three fast-acting levers identified for level management: glucose dosing (minutes), sludge extraction rate (hours), F/M adjustment through equalisation (hours, Fig. 9E)
Fast-acting levers allow operators to hold water level below 67% threshold during high-loading production without waiting for longer SRT adjustment cycle
C/N rises in rank for both TMP and flow; favorable band set by discharge schedule, reported as monitoring variable to be re-estimated periodically rather than fixed set-point

Recommendations in Table 4 supported by cross-model SHAP (Section 3.2, 16 models), conditional feasibility surface (manifold-constrained sample), and measured attainment rate with primary levers validated out-of-time
Convergence of model-based and measurement-based evidence distinguishes protocol from previous MBR optimization studies
